## Yes — demand exceeded the contract limit on 16 June

**Peak:** 1,324.4 kW at 08:15, which is 6% above the 1,250 kW contract [data: get_demand].

**Two intervals over contract:**
- 08:00 → 1,307.1 kW (57 kW over) — up to NT$5,106 penalty [data: get_demand]

**Cause:** A simultaneous start of 10 machines (805 kW rated) within 3 minutes at ~07:57–08:27, detected as a high-severity event [unverified citation removed]. This is the "Monday morning simultaneous start" scenario S2 [unverified citation removed].

**Avoidable with staggering:** Starting the machines 15 minutes apart would have cut the peak to 1,141.5 kW — below contract — avoiding up to NT$6,652 (US$208) in penalties [data: whatif_staggered_start].

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it is left on [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. That is a large continuous load producing nothing, which is exactly the "idle energy" the energy policy targets [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-01_energy_policy.md#EM-01 Energy Policy > Objectives > Objective 3: cut idle energy]. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

## Excess energy in incident S5

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]:

- Weekend energy: **~1,556 kWh** vs. **~346 kWh** normal
- **Excess: ~1,210 kWh** from that single oven

Note that the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit comes from switching the oven off proactively rather than detecting it afterward [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

answer:
According to the demand management playbook (EM-02), the load-shed order is:

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) — it is the first action because it has no effect on production, pausing it sheds 100% of its load immediately. [unverified citation removed]

The full shed order is:
1. **Pause EV charging** (EV-01) — 100% of load
2. Delay the next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02) — 35%
3. Raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02) — 4%
4. Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01, AC-02, AC-03) — 3.5%

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- Server room (DC-01) — a continuous critical load, never part of any load-shed action [unverified citation removed]
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03)

These are confirmed in both EM-02 and SOP-06. [unverified citation removed]
